You are migrating rule module docstrings in the `mlt` Rust project at /home/watermarkhu/repositories/mlt to a standardized documentation schema so that docs/scripts/gen_rules_docs.ts can generate documentation pages from them.

## The schema (MUST read first)
Read `docs/scripts/SCHEMA.md` in full — it defines the exact docstring format.

## Reference implementations (MUST read)
These two modules are already migrated correctly and are your ground truth:
- `crates/mlt_rules/src/nosemi.rs` (single-check flat rule)
- `crates/mlt_rules/src/bugs/mod.rs` (multi-check engine with `## Check IDs` table, `## Fix`, `## Examples`)

## Your modules (migrate ALL of them)
1. `crates/mlt_rules/src/syntax_errors/mod.rs` (meta ID `SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE`, category `syntax-errors`, severity Error)
2. `crates/mlt_rules/src/incomplete_analysis/mod.rs` (meta ID `INCOMPLETE_ANALYSIS`, category `incomplete-analysis`, severity Error)
3. `crates/mlt_rules/src/config_issues/mod.rs` (meta ID `CONFIG_ISSUES_ENGINE`, category `configuration-issues`, severity Error)
4. `crates/mlt_rules/src/unused/mod.rs` (meta ID `UNUSED_ENGINE`, category `unused-constructions`, severity Warning)
5. `crates/mlt_rules/src/unset_variables/mod.rs` (meta ID `UNSET_VARIABLES_ENGINE`, category `unset-variables`, severity Warning)

## Front-matter slugs (keep existing URLs)
Use these `slug` values so pages keep current filenames: `syntax-errors`, `incomplete-analysis`, `config-issues`, `unused`, `unset-variables`. Pick a sensible `icon` from the lucide set already used (see docs/.vitepress/theme/components/PageIcon.vue for the supported list, e.g. `lucide/x-circle`, `lucide/wrench`, `lucide/cog`, `lucide/trash-2`, `lucide/alert-triangle`).

## What to do
1. Read each module's current `//!` docstring and the `Rule` impl (`fn id`, `fn description`, `fn severity`, `fn category`, `fn check`, `fn check_file`, whether any `Diagnostic` has `fix: Some(...)`).
2. Rewrite the `//!` header to the schema format:
   - `# <META_ID>: <Title>` H1
   - ```mlt front-matter block with id/title/category/severity/fix/icon/slug
   - `## Rule` — what the engine does (prose)
   - `## Check IDs` — a `| Check ID | Severity | Fix | Description |` markdown table listing EVERY check ID the engine emits. **Verify the exact check IDs by grepping the Rust source for `rule_id:` literals** — do NOT trust the old docstring table blindly; add missing ones and fix stale ones. Determine per-check `severity` (usually the engine default) and `fix` (`yes` only if that check's emitted Diagnostic sets `fix: Some(...)`).
   - `## Fix` — ONLY if `fix = true` in front-matter (i.e. at least one check emits a fix). Describe the rewrites. Otherwise omit the section.
   - `## Examples` — with `### Incorrect` and `### Correct` MATLAB blocks covering representative checks. If the engine has auto-fixes, add a `### Fixed` with a diff.
   - Keep the existing `## Configuration` section (TOML) as-is after Examples.
3. Preserve any useful module-level prose (architecture notes, data-file descriptions) by folding it into `## Rule` or a `## Data File` section.
4. IMPORTANT: keep the `//!` doc comment valid Rust — it must start with `//!` on every line and end cleanly before the first `use`/`mod` statement. Do not add non-`//!` comments.

## Verification (mandatory)
For EACH migrated module run:
```
bun docs/scripts/gen_rules_docs.ts --check-module <slug>
```
It must exit 0. If it fails, fix the docstring and re-run. Note: other agents may be editing other modules concurrently, so only YOUR module's check result matters — ignore errors about other slugs.

Also run `cargo build` at the end to confirm the Rust still compiles.

Do NOT run the plain write mode `bun docs/scripts/gen_rules_docs.ts` (no --check-module), do NOT edit `docs/rules.md`, `docs/scripts/gen_rules_docs.ts`, `docs/scripts/SCHEMA.md`, or any file outside your five modules. Do NOT commit.

Return a summary of which check IDs each module now documents, and which checks have fixes.
Let me start by reading the schema and reference implementations.

# mlt Rule Documentation Schema

Every rule module in `crates/mlt_rules/src` documents itself through a
**standardized header docstring** written in markdown inside the Rust `//!`
module comment. `docs/scripts/gen_rules_docs.ts` reads these docstrings and
generates one documentation page per rule.

A *rule* is a module that self-registers with `inventory::submit!` — i.e. one
row in the "Rule" trait sense (e.g. `NOSEMI`, or a multi-check engine like
`BUGS_ENGINE`, `COMPAT`, `NAMING_ENGINE`). Each rule page anchors every check
ID the rule emits.

## Docstring Layout

Every rule docstring MUST follow this exact structure:

```text
//! # <META_ID>: <Human Title>
//!
//! ```mlt
//! id = "<META_ID>"                    # required — config/registration ID
//! title = "<Human Title>"             # required — shown as the page H1
//! category = "<category-slug>"        # required — Category::as_str()
//! severity = "<error|warning|info>"   # required — default severity
//! fix = <true|false>                  # required — does it auto-fix?
//! icon = "lucide/<name>"              # optional — page icon
//! slug = "<url-slug>"                 # optional — page filename stem
//! data_file = "<name>.toml"           # optional — data-driven engine
//! note = "..."                        # optional — italic callout line
//! ```
//!
//! ## Rule
//!
//! <free-form markdown: what the rule does, why it matters>
//!
//! ## Fix
//!
//! <free-form markdown: what the auto-fix rewrites; OMIT this section
//!  entirely when `fix = false`>
//!
//! ## Examples
//!
//! <free-form markdown with `Correct` / `Incorrect` / `Fixed` fenced
//!  matlab blocks>
```

Rules producing multiple check IDs (engines) add an optional fourth section
between `## Rule` and `## Fix`:

```text
//! ## Check IDs
//!
//! | Check ID | Severity | Fix | Description |
//! | -------- | -------- | --- | ----------- |
//! | CTRUE    | error    | no  | Condition is always true |
//! | CMDAND   | error    | yes | `&` where `&&` intended |
```

Data-driven engines (`data_file = "..."`) instead reference a TOML table in
`crates/mlt_rules/src/data/`; the generator builds the check-ID list from the
data file. See [Data-driven engines](#data-driven-engines).

## Front-matter keys (` ```mlt ` block)

| Key | Required | Type | Description |
| --- | -------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `id` | yes | string | Registration ID (e.g. `NOSEMI`, `BUGS_ENGINE`, `COMPAT`, `NAMING_ENGINE`). |
| `title` | yes | string | Human-readable title; becomes the page H1. |
| `category` | yes | string | Category slug from `Category::as_str()` (e.g. `bugs`, `formatting`, `compatibility`). |
| `severity` | yes | string | Default severity: `error`, `warning`, or `info`. |
| `fix` | yes | bool | Whether any emitted diagnostic carries an auto-fix. |
| `icon` | no | string | VitePress icon name (`lucide/bug`). Defaults to a category-derived icon. |
| `slug` | no | string | Page filename stem (default: `id` lowercased, `_` → `-`). |
| `data_file` | no | string | TOML data file name for data-driven engines. |
| `generated` | no | string | `naming` — engine check IDs are a computed product (see below). |
| `note` | no | string | One-line italic callout rendered under the H1. |

## `## Rule`

The primary section. Explain what the rule detects, the category it belongs
to, and — for engines — that one engine dispatches many check IDs. Keep it
prose; this becomes the page's "What this rule does" content.

## `## Check IDs`

Required for multi-check engines; omitted for single-check rules.

- Markdown table with exactly four columns: `Check ID | Severity | Fix | Description`.
- `Severity` is `error`, `warning`, or `info` (per-check override of the rule default).
- `Fix` is `yes` or `no` (does THIS check emit a fix).
- `Description` is a one-line summary; keep `|` escaped as `\|` if needed.

The generator turns each row into an anchor (`#<check-id>`) on the rule page,
and each row also feeds the global rule index in `docs/rules.md`.

## `## Fix`

Required **iff** `fix = true`. Describes what the auto-fix rewrites. Omit the
whole section when `fix = false`.

## `## Examples`

Required. Use `Correct` / `Incorrect` / `Fixed` sub-headings with fenced
`matlab` blocks. For engines, show representative examples covering several
check IDs.

## Data-driven engines

When `data_file` is present, the generator reads
`crates/mlt_rules/src/data/<data_file>` and builds the check-ID list from its
`[[checks]]` entries (`id`, `severity`, `message`, `category`, `function_name`).
The docstring omits the `## Check IDs` table; the generator substitutes an
anchored table grouped by the entries' `category` field.

The `naming` engine uses `generated = "naming"` instead: the generator computes
the 81 `naming.<entity>.<checkType>` check IDs as the Cartesian product of the
documented entity and check-type lists, so the docstring needs no table.

## Generator outputs

For each rule module the generator writes:

1. `docs/rules/<slug>.md` — the rule page. The `slug` is the front-matter
   `slug` key (or derived from `id`). Every check ID appears as an anchor so
   overviews can deep-link (`docs/rules/bugs.md#FNAN`).
2. A row (or rows, one per check ID) in the rule index table in
   `docs/rules.md`, linking to the rule page and anchors.

`--check` mode verifies every generated file is byte-identical to what the
sources produce, so the `hk` pre-commit hook fails on stale docs.
`--check-module <slug>` verifies a single rule page — useful while migrating
modules one at a time.

## Rules for writers

- Keep the `mlt` front-matter block byte-parseable: simple `key = "value"`
  lines, double-quoted strings, no comments inside the block.
- The front-matter `severity`/`category` MUST match the `Rule` impl's
  `fn severity()` / `fn category()`.
- Section headings are exact: `## Rule`, `## Check IDs`, `## Fix`, `## Examples`.
  Do not rename or add required-section variants.
- `## Configuration` (TOML example) is optional and may follow `## Examples`.
- `# <META_ID>: <Title>` H1 must contain the meta ID; the front-matter `title`
  may differ in wording but should be consistent.

1: //! # NOSEMI: Trailing Semicolon Missing
2: //!
3: //! ```mlt
4: //! id = "NOSEMI"
5: //! title = "Trailing Semicolon Missing"
6: //! category = "formatting"
7: //! severity = "info"
8: //! fix = true
9: //! icon = "lucide/code"
10: //! ```
11: //!
12: //! ## Rule
13: //!
14: //! Flags MATLAB statements that produce output without a trailing semicolon.
15: //! In MATLAB, such statements print their result to the console, which is
16: //! almost always unintentional in production code and can cause significant
17: //! performance degradation in loops.
18: //!
19: //! ## Fix
20: //!
21: //! Inserts a trailing semicolon immediately after the statement, suppressing
22: //! the console output without changing program behavior.
23: //!
24: //! ## Examples
25: //!
26: //! ### Incorrect
27: //!
28: //! ```matlab
29: //! x = compute_value()
30: //! data = load('file.mat')
31: //! ```
32: //!
33: //! ### Correct
34: //!
35: //! ```matlab
36: //! x = compute_value();
37: //! data = load('file.mat');
38: //! ```
39: //!
40: //! ### Fixed
41: //!
42: //! ```diff
43: //! - x = compute_value()
44: //! + x = compute_value();
45: //! ```
46: //!
47: //! ## Configuration
48: //!
49: //! ```toml
50: //! [lint.rules.NOSEMI]
51: //! severity = "info"
52: //! ignore_functions = ["disp", "fprintf", "warning", "error"]
53: //! ```
54: 
55: use mlt_core::{Category, Config, Diagnostic, Fix, NodeContext, Rule, Severity};
56: use serde::Deserialize;
57: 
58: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
59: // Rule-specific configuration
60: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
61: 
62: /// Configuration for NOSEMI.
63: ///
64: /// Deserialized from the `[lint.rules.NOSEMI]` section in `.mlt.toml`.
65: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Default)]
66: pub struct NosemiConfig {
67:     /// Function names to ignore (statements calling these functions won't be
68:     /// flagged even without a semicolon). Useful for intentional output
69:     /// functions like `disp`, `fprintf`, etc.
70:     #[serde(default)]
71:     pub ignore_functions: Vec<String>,
72: }
73: 
74: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
75: // Rule implementation
76: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
77: 
78: /// Rule NOSEMI: flags statements at the top level of a block that do not end
79: /// with a trailing semicolon.
80: ///
81: /// Targets `assignment`, `function_call`, and `command` nodes. Only fires when
82: /// the node is a direct child of `source_file` or `block` (i.e., at statement
83: /// level, not as a sub-expression).
84: pub struct Nosemi {
85:     config: NosemiConfig,
86: }
87: 
88: /// Statement-level node types that should typically end with a semicolon.
89: const TARGET_NODES: &[&str] = &["assignment", "function_call", "command"];
90: 
91: /// Parent node types that indicate statement-level context.
92: const STATEMENT_PARENTS: &[&str] = &["source_file", "block"];
93: 
94: impl Nosemi {
95:     /// Factory constructor. Reads rule-specific params from config.
96:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
97:         let rule_config: NosemiConfig = config.rule_params("NOSEMI");
98:         Box::new(Self {
99:             config: rule_config,
100:         })
101:     }
102: }
103: 
104: impl Rule for Nosemi {
105:     fn id(&self) -> &'static str {
106:         "NOSEMI"
107:     }
108: 
109:     fn description(&self) -> &'static str {
110:         "Statement without trailing semicolon may produce unintended console output"
111:     }
112: 
113:     fn severity(&self) -> Severity {
114:         Severity::Info
115:     }
116: 
117:     fn category(&self) -> Category {
118:         Category::Formatting
119:     }
120: 
121:     fn target_node_types(&self) -> &'static [&'static str] {
122:         TARGET_NODES
123:     }
124: 
125:     fn check(&self, ctx: &NodeContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
126:         let node = ctx.node;
127: 
128:         // Only fire at statement level: parent must be source_file or block.
129:         // This prevents flagging function_call nodes that are sub-expressions
130:         // (e.g., `x = foo(bar(1))` — bar(1) is not a statement).
131:         let is_statement_level = node
132:             .parent()
133:             .map(|p| STATEMENT_PARENTS.contains(&p.kind()))
134:             .unwrap_or(false);
135: 
136:         if !is_statement_level {
137:             return Vec::new();
138:         }
139: 
140:         // If this is a function_call or command, check if the function name
141:         // is in the ignore list.
142:         if !self.config.ignore_functions.is_empty() {
143:             if let Some(func_name) = extract_function_name(node, ctx.source) {
144:                 if self.config.ignore_functions.iter().any(|f| f == func_name) {
145:                     return Vec::new();
146:                 }
147:             }
148:         }
149: 
150:         // Check if the statement is followed by a semicolon.
151:         let has_semicolon = has_trailing_semicolon(node, ctx.source);
152: 
153:         if has_semicolon {
154:             return Vec::new();
155:         }
156: 
157:         // Compute position for the diagnostic.
158:         let start = node.start_position();
159:         let end_byte = node.end_byte();
160: 
161:         vec![Diagnostic {
162:             rule_id: self.id(),
163:             message: self.description().to_string(),
164:             severity: self.severity(),
165:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..end_byte,
166:             line: start.row + 1, // tree-sitter is 0-indexed
167:             column: start.column + 1,
168:             fix: Some(Fix::insert(end_byte, ";")),
169:         }]
170:     }
171: }
172: 
173: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
174: // Helpers
175: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
176: 
177: /// Extract the function name from a `function_call` or `command` node.
178: fn extract_function_name<'a>(node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
179:     match node.kind() {
180:         "function_call" => {
181:             // The `name` field of a function_call node.
182:             let name_node = node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
183:             // For simple calls, the name is an identifier.
184:             // For method calls (obj.method), take the full text.
185:             Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
186:         }
187:         "command" => {
188:             // The first child of a command is the command_name.
189:             let name_node = node.child(0)?;
190:             if name_node.kind() == "command_name" {
191:                 Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()])
192:             } else {
193:                 None
194:             }
195:         }
196:         _ => None,
197:     }
198: }
199: 
200: /// Determine whether a statement node is followed by a semicolon.
201: ///
202: /// In tree-sitter-matlab's grammar, semicolons (`;`) and newlines are statement
203: /// terminators that appear as sibling nodes after the statement. We check the
204: /// source text immediately following the node for a `;` (skipping whitespace
205: /// on the same line).
206: fn has_trailing_semicolon(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
207:     // Strategy 1: Check next named/unnamed siblings for ";"
208:     let mut sibling = node.next_sibling();
209:     while let Some(sib) = sibling {
210:         let kind = sib.kind();
211:         // Skip over comment nodes that might appear between statement and semicolon
212:         if kind == "comment" || kind == "line_continuation" {
213:             sibling = sib.next_sibling();
214:             continue;
215:         }
216:         // If the next meaningful sibling is ";", the statement is terminated.
217:         if kind == ";" {
218:             return true;
219:         }
220:         // Any other sibling means no semicolon follows.
221:         break;
222:     }
223: 
224:     // Strategy 2: Fallback — scan the source text after the node end.
225:     // This handles cases where the semicolon might not be a separate node.
226:     let after = &source[node.end_byte()..];
227:     for ch in after.chars() {
228:         match ch {
229:             ';' => return true,
230:             // Stop at newline — semicolon must be on the same line.
231:             '\n' | '\r' => return false,
232:             // Skip inline whitespace.
233:             ' ' | '\t' => continue,
234:             // Any other character means something else follows.
235:             _ => return false,
236:         }
237:     }
238: 
239:     false
240: }

401:     fn check_switch_no_otherwise(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
402:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
403:         Self::walk_switch_no_otherwise(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
404:         diagnostics
405:     }
406: 
407:     fn walk_switch_no_otherwise(node: Node, _source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
408:         if node.kind() == "switch_statement" {
409:             let mut has_otherwise = false;
410:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
411:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
412:                 if child.kind() == "otherwise_clause" {
413:                     has_otherwise = true;
414:                     break;
415:                 }
416:             }
417: 
418:             if !has_otherwise {
419:                 let pos = node.start_position();
420:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
421:                     rule_id: "NOPRC",
422:                     message: "Switch statement has no 'otherwise' clause".to_string(),
423:                     severity: Severity::Error,
424:                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
425:                     line: pos.row + 1,
426:                     column: pos.column + 1,
427:                     fix: None,
428:                 });
429:             }
430:         }
431: 
432:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
433:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
434:             Self::walk_switch_no_otherwise(child, _source, diagnostics);
435:         }
436:     }

438:     /// MEXCEP: Catch clause without an exception identifier.
439:     fn check_catch_without_id(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
440:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
441:         Self::walk_catch_without_id(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
442:         diagnostics
443:     }
444: 
445:     fn walk_catch_without_id(node: Node, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
446:         if node.kind() == "catch_clause" {
447:             // Check if the catch clause has an identifier child.
448:             let has_id = {
449:                 let mut cursor = node.walk();
450:                 let result = node.children(&mut cursor).any(|c| c.kind() == "identifier");
451:                 result
452:             };
453: 
454:             if !has_id {
455:                 // Also check the source text for `catch <id>` pattern.
456:                 let catch_text = node_text(node, source).trim().to_string();
457:                 let has_id_text = catch_text
458:                     .strip_prefix("catch")
459:                     .map(|rest| {
460:                         let rest = rest.trim();
461:                         !rest.is_empty() && rest.chars().next().is_some_and(|c| c.is_alphabetic())
462:                     })
463:                     .unwrap_or(false);
464: 
465:                 if !has_id_text {
466:                     let pos = node.start_position();
467:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
468:                         rule_id: "MEXCEP",
469:                         message: "Catch clause without exception identifier; exceptions will be silently ignored".to_string(),
470:                         severity: Severity::Error,
471:                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
472:                         line: pos.row + 1,
473:                         column: pos.column + 1,
474:                         fix: None,
475:                     });
476:                 }
477:             }
478:         }
479: 
480:         // For try_statement, check its catch_clause children.
481:         if node.kind() == "try_statement" {
482:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
483:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
484:                 if child.kind() == "catch_clause" {
485:                     Self::walk_catch_without_id(child, source, diagnostics);
486:                 }
487:             }
488:         }
489: 
490:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
491:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
492:             if child.kind() != "catch_clause" {
493:                 Self::walk_catch_without_id(child, source, diagnostics);
494:             }
495:         }
496:     }

498:     /// RHSFN: Function name used on RHS without `@` handle prefix.
499:     ///
500:     /// Detects when a known MATLAB builtin function name is used as a variable
501:     /// (identifier) on the right-hand side of an assignment without `@`.
502:     fn check_rhs_function_name(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
503:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
504:         // Collect function definitions in this file.
505:         let defined_functions = collect_defined_functions(root, source);
506:         Self::walk_rhs_function_name(root, source, &defined_functions, &mut diagnostics);
507:         diagnostics
508:     }
509: 
510:     fn walk_rhs_function_name(
511:         node: Node,
512:         source: &str,
513:         defined_functions: &HashSet<String>,
514:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
515:     ) {
516:         if node.kind() == "assignment" {
517:             // Check the RHS for bare function name usage.
518:             if let Some(rhs) = node.child_by_field_name("right").or_else(|| node.child(2)) {
519:                 if rhs.kind() == "identifier" {
520:                     let name = node_text(rhs, source).trim();
521:                     // Only flag if the name matches a known defined function.
522:                     if defined_functions.contains(name) {
523:                         let pos = rhs.start_position();
524:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
525:                             rule_id: "RHSFN",
526:                             message: format!(
527:                                 "Function name '{name}' used without '@'; did you mean '@{name}'?"
528:                             ),
529:                             severity: Severity::Error,
530:                             byte_range: rhs.start_byte()..rhs.end_byte(),
531:                             line: pos.row + 1,
532:                             column: pos.column + 1,
533:                             fix: Some(Fix::new(
534:                                 rhs.start_byte()..rhs.end_byte(),
535:                                 format!("@{name}"),
536:                             )),
537:                         });
538:                     }
539:                 }
540:             }
541:         }
542: 
543:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
544:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
545:             Self::walk_rhs_function_name(child, source, defined_functions, diagnostics);
546:         }
547:     }

549:     /// VARARG: Misuse of varargin/varargout.
550:     ///
551:     /// Flags usage of `varargin` outside a function that declares it, or
552:     /// `varargout` in a function that doesn't have it as an output.
553:     fn check_vararg_misuse(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
554:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
555:         Self::walk_vararg_misuse(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
556:         diagnostics
557:     }
558: 
559:     fn walk_vararg_misuse(node: Node, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
560:         if node.kind() == "function_definition" {
561:             let func_text = node_text(node, source);
562:             let has_varargin_param = func_text.contains("varargin");
563:             let has_varargout_output = func_text.contains("varargout");
564: 
565:             // Check body for varargin/varargout usage.
566:             Self::check_vararg_in_body(
567:                 node,
568:                 source,
569:                 has_varargin_param,
570:                 has_varargout_output,
571:                 diagnostics,
572:             );
573:         }
574: 
575:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
576:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
577:             if child.kind() != "function_definition" {
578:                 Self::walk_vararg_misuse(child, source, diagnostics);
579:             }
580:         }
581:     }
582: 
583:     fn check_vararg_in_body(
584:         node: Node,
585:         source: &str,
586:         has_varargin: bool,
587:         has_varargout: bool,
588:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
589:     ) {
590:         if node.kind() == "identifier" {
591:             let name = node_text(node, source).trim();
592:             if name == "varargin" && !has_varargin {
593:                 let pos = node.start_position();
594:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
595:                     rule_id: "VARARG",
596:                     message: "'varargin' used in function that does not declare it as input"
597:                         .to_string(),
598:                     severity: Severity::Error,
599:                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
600:                     line: pos.row + 1,
601:                     column: pos.column + 1,
602:                     fix: None,
603:                 });
604:             } else if name == "varargout" && !has_varargout {
605:                 let pos = node.start_position();
606:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
607:                     rule_id: "VARARG",
608:                     message: "'varargout' used in function that does not declare it as output"
609:                         .to_string(),
610:                     severity: Severity::Error,
611:                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
612:                     line: pos.row + 1,
613:                     column: pos.column + 1,
614:                     fix: None,
615:                 });
616:             }
617:         }
618: 
619:         // Don't recurse into nested function definitions.
620:         if node.kind() == "function_definition" {
621:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
622:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
623:                 if child.kind() != "function_definition" {
624:                     Self::check_vararg_in_body(
625:                         child,
626:                         source,
627:                         has_varargin,
628:                         has_varargout,
629:                         diagnostics,
630:                     );
631:                 }
632:             }
633:         } else {
634:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
635:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
636:                 Self::check_vararg_in_body(child, source, has_varargin, has_varargout, diagnostics);
637:             }
638:         }
639:     }

641:     /// Parfor-related checks: PFUIXE, PFBFN, PFWHOS, PFTUSE, PFRNC.
642:     fn check_parfor_issues(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
643:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
644:         Self::walk_parfor_issues(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
645:         diagnostics
646:     }
647: 
648:     fn walk_parfor_issues(node: Node, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
649:         if node.kind() == "for_statement" {
650:             let stmt_text = node_text(node, source);
651:             if !stmt_text.starts_with("parfor") {
652:                 // Not a parfor — check if it could be one (FWPARF).
653:                 if could_be_parfor(node, source) {
654:                     let pos = node.start_position();
655:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
656:                         rule_id: "FWPARF",
657:                         message:
658:                             "For loop could potentially be converted to parfor for parallelism"
659:                                 .to_string(),
660:                         severity: Severity::Error,
661:                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
662:                         line: pos.row + 1,
663:                         column: pos.column + 1,
664:                         fix: None,
665:                     });
666:                 }
667: 
668:                 // Recurse into children.
669:                 let mut cursor = node.walk();
670:                 for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
671:                     Self::walk_parfor_issues(child, source, diagnostics);
672:                 }
673:                 return;
674:             }
675: 
676:             // This is a parfor. Extract the loop variable.
677:             let loop_var = extract_for_variable(node, source);
678: 
679:             // Walk the parfor body for issues.
680:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
681:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
682:                 if child.kind() == "block" {
683:                     Self::check_parfor_body(child, source, loop_var.as_deref(), diagnostics);
684:                 }
685:             }
686: 
687:             // PFTRIV: Check if parfor could just be a for loop (body is trivial).
688:             if is_trivial_parfor(node, source) {
689:                 let pos = node.start_position();
690:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
691:                     rule_id: "PFTRIV",
692:                     message: "Parfor loop body is trivial; consider using regular for loop"
693:                         .to_string(),
694:                     severity: Severity::Error,
695:                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
696:                     line: pos.row + 1,
697:                     column: pos.column + 1,
698:                     fix: None,
699:                 });
700:             }
701:         }
702: 
703:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
704:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
705:             Self::walk_parfor_issues(child, source, diagnostics);
706:         }
707:     }
708: 
709:     fn check_parfor_body(
710:         node: Node,
711:         source: &str,
712:         loop_var: Option<&str>,
713:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
714:     ) {
715:         match node.kind() {
716:             "function_call" => {
717:                 let func_name = extract_call_name(node, source);
718:                 if let Some(name) = &func_name {
719:                     // PFUIXE: Loop variable used in eval.
720:                     if *name == "eval" || *name == "evalin" || *name == "feval" {
721:                         if let Some(lv) = loop_var {
722:                             let args = collect_call_args(node, source);
723:                             if args.iter().any(|a| a.contains(lv)) {
724:                                 let pos = node.start_position();
725:                                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
726:                                     rule_id: "PFUIXE",
727:                                     message: format!(
728:                                         "Parfor index variable '{lv}' used in {name}; \
729:                                          this is not allowed in parfor"
730:                                     ),
731:                                     severity: Severity::Error,
732:                                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
733:                                     line: pos.row + 1,
734:                                     column: pos.column + 1,
735:                                     fix: None,
736:                                 });
737:                             }
738:                         }
739:                     }
740: 
741:                     // PFWHOS: who/whos in parfor.
742:                     if *name == "who" || *name == "whos" {
743:                         let pos = node.start_position();
744:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
745:                             rule_id: "PFWHOS",
746:                             message: format!("'{name}' is not allowed inside parfor loops"),
747:                             severity: Severity::Error,
748:                             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
749:                             line: pos.row + 1,
750:                             column: pos.column + 1,
751:                             fix: None,
752:                         });
753:                     }
754: 
755:                     // PFBFN: Certain builtin functions problematic in parfor.
756:                     let problematic_builtins = [
757:                         "assignin",
758:                         "evalin",
759:                         "save",
760:                         "load",
761:                         "clear",
762:                         "global",
763:                         "persistent",
764:                     ];
765:                     if problematic_builtins.contains(name) {
766:                         let pos = node.start_position();
767:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
768:                             rule_id: "PFBFN",
769:                             message: format!(
770:                                 "Function '{name}' may not behave as expected inside parfor"
771:                             ),
772:                             severity: Severity::Error,
773:                             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
774:                             line: pos.row + 1,
775:                             column: pos.column + 1,
776:                             fix: None,
777:                         });
778:                     }
779:                 }
780:             }
781:             "assignment" => {
782:                 // PFTUSE / PFRNC: Check for temporary variable misuse and
783:                 // inconsistent reduction patterns.
784:                 if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left").or_else(|| node.child(0)) {
785:                     if lhs.kind() == "identifier" {
786:                         let var_name = node_text(lhs, source).trim().to_string();
787:                         if let Some(rhs) =
788:                             node.child_by_field_name("right").or_else(|| node.child(2))
789:                         {
790:                             let rhs_text = node_text(rhs, source);
791:                             // PFTUSE: Variable used on both sides but is not a reduction.
792:                             if rhs_text.contains(&var_name)
793:                                 && !is_reduction_pattern(&var_name, rhs, source)
794:                             {
795:                                 let pos = node.start_position();
796:                                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
797:                                     rule_id: "PFTUSE",
798:                                     message: format!(
799:                                         "Temporary variable '{var_name}' used on both sides of \
800:                                          assignment in parfor; ensure correct classification"
801:                                     ),
802:                                     severity: Severity::Error,
803:                                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
804:                                     line: pos.row + 1,
805:                                     column: pos.column + 1,
806:                                     fix: None,
807:                                 });
808:                             }
809: 
810:                             // PFRNC: Reduction operator not consistent.
811:                             if is_reduction_pattern(&var_name, rhs, source) {
812:                                 // Check for mixed reduction operators on same variable.
813:                                 // This is a simplified check — full analysis would track
814:                                 // across the entire parfor body.
815:                                 if has_mixed_reduction_ops(&var_name, rhs, source) {
816:                                     let pos = node.start_position();
817:                                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
818:                                         rule_id: "PFRNC",
819:                                         message: format!(
820:                                             "Reduction variable '{var_name}' uses inconsistent \
821:                                              operators in parfor"
822:                                         ),
823:                                         severity: Severity::Error,
824:                                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
825:                                         line: pos.row + 1,
826:                                         column: pos.column + 1,
827:                                         fix: None,
828:                                     });
829:                                 }
830:                             }
831:                         }
832:                     }
833:                 }
834:             }
835:             _ => {}
836:         }
837: 
838:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
839:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
840:             Self::check_parfor_body(child, source, loop_var, diagnostics);
841:         }
842:     }
843: }

867:         TARGET_NODES
868:     }

878:     fn check(&self, ctx: &NodeContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
879:         let node = ctx.node;
880:         let source = ctx.source;
881:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
882: 
883:         match node.kind() {
884:             "if_statement" | "while_statement" => {
885:                 diagnostics.extend(self.check_constant_condition(node, source));
886:             }
887:             "boolean_operator" => {
888:                 diagnostics.extend(self.check_short_circuit(node, source));
889:                 diagnostics.extend(self.check_duplicate_conditions(node, source));
890:             }
891:             "binary_operator" => {
892:                 diagnostics.extend(self.check_element_wise_boolean(node, source));
893:                 diagnostics.extend(self.check_scalar_array_op(node, source));
894:                 diagnostics.extend(self.check_operator_precedence(node, source));
895:             }
896:             "comparison_operator" => {
897:                 diagnostics.extend(self.check_nan_comparison(node, source));
898:                 diagnostics.extend(self.check_length_empty(node, source));
899:                 diagnostics.extend(self.check_size_comparison(node, source));
900:             }
901:             "function_call" => {
902:                 diagnostics.extend(self.check_debug_function(node, source));
903:                 diagnostics.extend(self.check_strcmpi_same_case(node, source));
904:                 diagnostics.extend(self.check_strcmp_char(node, source));
905:                 diagnostics.extend(self.check_funfun(node, source));
906:                 diagnostics.extend(self.check_assert_constant(node, source));
907:             }
908:             "assignment" => {
909:                 diagnostics.extend(self.check_self_modify(node, source));
910:             }
911:             // switch_statement and try_statement are handled at file level.
912:             _ => {}
913:         }
914: 
915:         diagnostics
916:     }

918:     fn check_file(&self, ctx: &FileContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
919:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
920:         let root = ctx.tree.root_node();
921:         let source = ctx.source;
922: 
923:         // File-level checks.
924:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_if_branch_dup_bodies(root, source));
925:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_if_condition_dup(root, source));
926:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_switch_dup_cases(root, source));
927:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_switch_no_otherwise(root, source));
928:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_catch_without_id(root, source));
929:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_rhs_function_name(root, source));
930:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_vararg_misuse(root, source));
931:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_parfor_issues(root, source));
932: 
933:         diagnostics
934:     }

941: /// Extract the text of a node from the source.
942: pub(crate) fn node_text<'a>(node: Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
943:     &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()]
944: }
945: 
946: /// Normalize whitespace in a string for comparison purposes.
947: pub(crate) fn normalize_whitespace(s: &str) -> String {
948:     s.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ")
949: }
950: 
951: /// Find the condition child of an `if_statement` or `elseif_clause` node.
952: ///
953: /// In tree-sitter-matlab, the condition is typically the node between the
954: /// keyword (`if`/`elseif`/`while`) and the body.
955: pub(crate) fn find_condition_child(node: Node) -> Option<Node> {
956:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
957:     let mut found_keyword = false;
958:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
959:         if child.kind() == "if"
960:             || child.kind() == "elseif"
961:             || child.kind() == "while"
962:             || child.is_named() && found_keyword
963:         {
964:             if found_keyword && child.kind() != "block" && child.kind() != "end" {
965:                 return Some(child);
966:             }
967:             if !child.is_named() || child.kind() == "if" || child.kind() == "while" {
968:                 found_keyword = true;
969:             }
970:         }
971:     }
972: 
973:     // Fallback: return the first named child that is not a keyword or block.
974:     let mut cursor2 = node.walk();
975:     let result = node.children(&mut cursor2).find(|child| {
976:         child.is_named()
977:             && child.kind() != "block"
978:             && child.kind() != "elseif_clause"
979:             && child.kind() != "else_clause"
980:             && child.kind() != "end"
981:             && child.kind() != "comment"
982:     });
983:     result
984: }
985: 
986: /// Find a `block` child of a node.
987: pub(crate) fn find_block_child(node: Node) -> Option<Node> {
988:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
989:     let result = node
990:         .children(&mut cursor)
991:         .find(|child| child.kind() == "block");
992:     result
993: }
994: 
995: /// Find the case value node inside a `case_clause`.
996: pub(crate) fn find_case_value(case_node: Node) -> Option<Node> {
997:     let mut cursor = case_node.walk();
998:     let result = case_node
999:         .children(&mut cursor)
1000:         .find(|child| child.is_named() && child.kind() != "block" && child.kind() != "comment");
1001:     result
1002: }
1003: 
1004: /// Check if a condition text represents an always-true value.
1005: pub(crate) fn is_always_true(text: &str) -> bool {
1006:     let trimmed = text.trim();
1007:     trimmed == "true" || trimmed == "1" || trimmed == "1.0"
1008: }
1009: 
1010: /// Check if a condition text represents an always-false value.
1011: pub(crate) fn is_always_false(text: &str) -> bool {
1012:     let trimmed = text.trim();

315:     /// that starts with a block-opening keyword).
316:     pub(crate) fn classify_missing_end(

318:         source: &str,

320:         let start = node.start_byte();
321:         let node_end = node.end_byte().min(source.len());
322:         let text = &source[start..node_end];
323:         let lower = text.to_lowercase();
324:         let line = node.start_position().row + 1;
325: 
326:         // ENDCT4: ERROR text contains "classdef", a function_definition
327:         // follows it as a sibling, and no "methods" appears between them.
328:         if lower.contains("classdef") {
329:             let mut sibling = node.next_sibling();
330:             while let Some(sib) = sibling {
331:                 if sib.kind() == "function_definition" && sib.start_byte() > start {
332:                     let between = &source[node_end..sib.start_byte()];
333:                     if !between.to_lowercase().contains("methods") {
334:                         return Some((
335:                             "ENDCT4",
336:                             "A METHODS block or END might be missing before the function definition. This might be causing additional error messages.".to_string(),
337:                         ));
338:                     }
339:                     break;
340:                 }
341:                 sibling = sib.next_sibling();
342:             }
343:         }
344: 
345:         // ENDCT2: a block opener appears in the ERROR text or its previous
346:         // sibling, and the ERROR does not contain `end`.
347:         let has_end = lower.contains("end");
348:         if !has_end {
349:             let opener_in_text = BLOCK_OPENERS.iter().any(|kw| lower.contains(kw));
350:             let opener_in_prev = node
351:                 .prev_sibling()
352:                 .map(|prev| {
353:                     let prev_text = &source[prev.start_byte()..prev.end_byte()];
354:                     BLOCK_OPENERS
355:                         .iter()
356:                         .any(|kw| prev_text.to_lowercase().contains(kw))
357:                 })
358:                 .unwrap_or(false);
359:             if opener_in_text || opener_in_prev {
360:                 let raw_end = node.end_position().row;
361:                 let end_line = if source[..node_end].ends_with('\n') {
362:                     raw_end
363:                 } else {
364:                     raw_end + 1
365:                 };
366:                 let opener_line = if opener_in_text {
367:                     line
368:                 } else {
369:                     node.prev_sibling()
370:                         .map(|p| p.start_position().row + 1)
371:                         .unwrap_or(line)
372:                 };
373:                 return Some((
374:                     "ENDCT2",
375:                     format!(
376:                         "An END might be missing (after line {end_line}), possibly matching line {opener_line}."
377:                     ),
378:                 ));
379:             }
380:         }
381: 
382:         // ENDCT3: the ERROR is followed by a sibling that starts with a
383:         // block-opening keyword.
384:         let mut sibling = node.next_sibling();
385:         while let Some(sib) = sibling {
386:             let sib_text = &source[sib.start_byte()..sib.end_byte()];
387:             match sib_text.split_whitespace().next() {

392:                         "ENDCT3",

394:                             "An END might be missing (before {kw} on line {line}), possibly matching {matched}."
395:                         ),
396:                     ));
397:                 }
398:                 Some(_) => break,
399:                 None => {}
400:             }
401:             sibling = sib.next_sibling();
402:         }

404:         None

569:     /// Parse a hex or binary literal into (is_hex, digit count, type suffix).
570:     pub(crate) fn parse_hex_binary_literal(text: &str) -> Option<(bool, usize, Option<&str>)> {
571:         let (is_hex, rest) = if text.starts_with("0x") || text.starts_with("0X") {
572:             (true, &text[2..])
573:         } else if text.starts_with("0b") || text.starts_with("0B") {
574:             (false, &text[2..])
575:         } else {
576:             return None;
577:         };
578: 
579:         if rest.is_empty() {
580:             return None;
581:         }
582: 
583:         let suffix = if rest.len() >= 3 && Self::suffix_bits(&rest[rest.len() - 3..]).is_some() {
584:             Some(&rest[rest.len() - 3..])
585:         } else if rest.len() >= 2 && Self::suffix_bits(&rest[rest.len() - 2..]).is_some() {
586:             Some(&rest[rest.len() - 2..])
587:         } else {
588:             None
589:         };
590: 
591:         let digits = match suffix {
592:             Some(s) => &rest[..rest.len() - s.len()],
593:             None => rest,
594:         };
595: 
596:         if digits.is_empty() {

1: //! # Incomplete Analysis: Linter-Internal Limit Checks
2: //!
3: //! This module implements the 17 "Incomplete Analysis" checks from MATLAB's Code
4: //! Analyzer. These are special internal-limit diagnostics that **cannot be disabled**
5: //! by the user. They all have default severity `Error`.
6: //!
7: //! ## Check IDs
8: //!
9: //! | Check ID | Description                                  | Detection                                  |
10: //! |----------|----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
11: //! | TMMSG    | More than 10,000 diagnostics generated       | Post-lint (diagnostic count > threshold)   |
12: //! | TMSMS    | More than 1,000 parse errors generated       | Count ERROR nodes in tree                  |
13: //! | MXASET   | File too complex to analyze                  | Node count > threshold                     |
14: //! | QUIT     | Analysis did not complete                    | Engine panic guard (`catch_unwind` in `Linter::lint`) |
15: //! | NOSPC    | File too complex (nesting)                   | Max nesting depth > threshold              |
16: //! | MBIG     | File too large                               | Source length > threshold                  |
17: //! | NOFIL    | File not found                               | No-op (handled by CLI)                     |
18: //! | MDOTM    | Invalid file extension                       | File extension != `.m`                     |
19: //! | MDMCR    | Deployed MATLAB file                         | File extension == `.ctf` or `.p`           |
20: //! | RDERR    | Unable to read file                          | No-op (handled by CLI)                     |
21: //! | EOFER    | Too many syntax errors                       | ERROR node count > threshold               |
22: //! | EOFMI    | Incomplete file                              | Last node is ERROR or MISSING              |
23: //! | MDEEP    | Parentheses/brackets nested too deeply       | Max `()`, `[]`, `{}` nesting depth         |
24: //! | DEEPC    | Block comments nested too deeply             | Nested `%{ %}` detection                   |
25: //! | DEEPN    | Functions nested too deeply                  | Nested `function_definition` depth         |
26: //! | DEEPS    | Statements nested too deeply                 | Nested if/for/while/switch/try depth       |
27: //! | TEXTL    | Text too long                                | Max line length > threshold                |
28: //!
29: //! ## Configuration
30: //!
31: //! ```toml
32: //! [lint.rules.INCOMPLETE_ANALYSIS]
33: //! max_diagnostics = 10000
34: //! max_parse_errors = 1000
35: //! max_node_count = 100000
36: //! max_file_size = 1048576
37: //! max_paren_depth = 32
38: //! max_function_depth = 20
39: //! max_statement_depth = 15
40: //! max_line_length = 4096
41: //! ```

45: //! The engine, shared tree-walking infrastructure, and `check_file` dispatch live
46: //! in this `mod.rs`; each individual check lives in its own `check_*.rs` submodule.
47:

49: mod check_diagnostic_count;

52: mod check_function_depth;
53: mod check_incomplete_file;

98: /// Configuration for incomplete analysis checks — each threshold is configurable.
99: ///
100: /// Deserialized from the `[lint.rules.INCOMPLETE_ANALYSIS]` section in `.mlt.toml`.
101: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
102: pub struct IncompleteAnalysisConfig {
103:     /// Maximum number of diagnostics before TMMSG fires.
104:     #[serde(default = "default_max_diagnostics")]
105:     pub max_diagnostics: usize,
106: 
107:     /// Maximum parse error (ERROR node) count before TMSMS fires.
108:     #[serde(default = "default_max_parse_errors")]
109:     pub max_parse_errors: usize,
110: 
111:     /// Maximum tree node count before MXASET fires.
112:     #[serde(default = "default_max_node_count")]
113:     pub max_node_count: usize,
114: 
115:     /// Maximum source file size in bytes before MBIG fires.
116:     #[serde(default = "default_max_file_size")]
117:     pub max_file_size: usize,
118: 
119:     /// Maximum parentheses/bracket nesting depth before MDEEP fires.
120:     #[serde(default = "default_max_paren_depth")]
121:     pub max_paren_depth: usize,
122: 
123:     /// Maximum nested `function_definition` depth before DEEPN fires.
124:     #[serde(default = "default_max_function_depth")]
125:     pub max_function_depth: usize,
126: 
127:     /// Maximum nested statement (if/for/while/switch/try) depth before DEEPS fires.
128:     #[serde(default = "default_max_statement_depth")]
129:     pub max_statement_depth: usize,
130: 
131:     /// Maximum line length in characters before TEXTL fires.
132:     #[serde(default = "default_max_line_length")]
133:     pub max_line_length: usize,
134: }

136: impl Default for IncompleteAnalysisConfig {
137:     fn default() -> Self {
138:         Self {
139:             max_diagnostics: default_max_diagnostics(),
140:             max_parse_errors: default_max_parse_errors(),
141:             max_node_count: default_max_node_count(),
142:             max_file_size: default_max_file_size(),
143:             max_paren_depth: default_max_paren_depth(),
144:             max_function_depth: default_max_function_depth(),
145:             max_statement_depth: default_max_statement_depth(),
146:             max_line_length: default_max_line_length(),
147:         }

151: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
152: // Metrics collected during tree traversal
153: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
154: 
155: /// Metrics gathered in a single traversal of the parse tree.
156: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
157: pub(crate) struct TreeMetrics {
158:     /// Total number of nodes in the tree.
159:     node_count: usize,
160:     /// Number of ERROR nodes.
161:     error_count: usize,
162:     /// Maximum depth of parentheses/bracket nesting (`(`, `[`, `{`).
163:     max_paren_depth: usize,
164:     /// Maximum depth of nested `function_definition` nodes.
165:     max_function_depth: usize,
166:     /// Maximum depth of nested statement nodes (if/for/while/switch/try).
167:     max_statement_depth: usize,
168:     /// Whether the last child of the root is an ERROR or MISSING node.
169:     last_node_is_error: bool,
170: }
171: 
172: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
173: // Rule implementation
174: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
175: 
176: /// Incomplete Analysis Engine: a file-level rule that handles all 17
177: /// incomplete-analysis checks in a single pass.
178: ///
179: /// These checks represent linter-internal limits and cannot be disabled
180: /// by the user (`can_be_disabled() == false`).
181: pub struct IncompleteAnalysisEngine {
182:     config: IncompleteAnalysisConfig,
183: }
184: 
185: impl IncompleteAnalysisEngine {
186:     /// Factory constructor. Reads rule-specific params from config.
187:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
188:         let rule_config: IncompleteAnalysisConfig = config.rule_params("INCOMPLETE_ANALYSIS");
189:         Box::new(Self {
190:             config: rule_config,
191:         })
192:     }
193: 
194:     /// Walk the tree and collect all metrics in one pass.
195:     fn collect_metrics(&self, root: Node) -> TreeMetrics {
196:         let mut metrics = TreeMetrics::default();
197: 
198:         // Check last child of root for EOFMI.
199:         if let Some(last) = last_descendant(root) {
200:             metrics.last_node_is_error = last.is_error() || last.is_missing();
201:         }
202: 
203:         Self::walk_tree(root, &mut metrics, 0, 0, 0);
204:         metrics
205:     }
206: 
207:     /// Recursive DFS traversal that collects node counts, error counts, and
208:     /// nesting depths in a single pass.
209:     fn walk_tree(
210:         node: Node,
211:         metrics: &mut TreeMetrics,
212:         paren_depth: usize,
213:         function_depth: usize,
214:         statement_depth: usize,
215:     ) {
216:         metrics.node_count += 1;
217: 
218:         if node.is_error() {
219:             metrics.error_count += 1;
220:         }
221: 
222:         // Track parentheses/bracket nesting depth (MDEEP).
223:         let new_paren_depth = match node.kind() {
224:             "parenthesis" | "arguments" | "matrix" | "cell" => {
225:                 let d = paren_depth + 1;
226:                 if d > metrics.max_paren_depth {
227:                     metrics.max_paren_depth = d;
228:                 }
229:                 d
230:             }
231:             _ => paren_depth,
232:         };
233: 
234:         // Track function nesting depth (DEEPN).
235:         let new_function_depth = if node.kind() == "function_definition" {
236:             let d = function_depth + 1;
237:             if d > metrics.max_function_depth {
238:                 metrics.max_function_depth = d;
239:             }
240:             d
241:         } else {
242:             function_depth
243:         };
244: 
245:         // Track statement nesting depth (DEEPS).
246:         let new_statement_depth = match node.kind() {
247:             "if_statement" | "for_statement" | "while_statement" | "switch_statement"
248:             | "try_statement" => {
249:                 let d = statement_depth + 1;
250:                 if d > metrics.max_statement_depth {
251:                     metrics.max_statement_depth = d;
252:                 }
253:                 d
254:             }
255:             _ => statement_depth,
256:         };
257: 
258:         // Recurse into children.
259:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
260:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
261:             Self::walk_tree(
262:                 child,
263:                 metrics,
264:                 new_paren_depth,
265:                 new_function_depth,
266:                 new_statement_depth,
267:             );
268:         }
269:     }
270: }
271: 
272: impl Rule for IncompleteAnalysisEngine {
273:     fn id(&self) -> &'static str {
274:         "INCOMPLETE_ANALYSIS"
275:     }
276: 
277:     fn description(&self) -> &'static str {
278:         "Internal linter limits and analysis integrity checks"
279:     }
280: 
281:     fn severity(&self) -> Severity {
282:         Severity::Error
283:     }
284: 
285:     fn category(&self) -> Category {
286:         Category::IncompleteAnalysis
287:     }
288: 
289:     fn target_node_types(&self) -> &'static [&'static str] {
290:         // File-level only — no node subscriptions.
291:         &[]
292:     }
293: 
294:     fn can_be_disabled(&self) -> bool {
295:         false
296:     }
297: 
298:     fn has_file_check(&self) -> bool {
299:         true
300:     }
301: 
302:     fn check_file(&self, ctx: &FileContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
303:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
304:         let root = ctx.tree.root_node();
305:         let source = ctx.source;
306: 
307:         // -- Checks that don't need tree traversal --
308: 
309:         // MBIG: File too large.
310:         self.check_file_size(source, &mut diagnostics);
311: 
312:         // MDOTM: Invalid file extension (not .m).
313:         self.check_extension(ctx, source, &mut diagnostics);
314: 
315:         // -- Single-pass tree traversal --
316: 
317:         let metrics = self.collect_metrics(root);
318: 
319:         // MXASET: File too complex to analyze (node count).
320:         self.check_node_count(&metrics, source, &mut diagnostics);
321: 
322:         // TMSMS: Too many parse errors.
323:         // EOFER: Too many syntax errors (same as TMSMS but lower threshold).
324:         // Fires when error count exceeds max_parse_errors (same metric, distinct ID
325:         // for MATLAB compatibility).
326:         self.check_parse_errors(&metrics, source, &mut diagnostics);
327: 
328:         // NOSPC: File too complex (nesting) — uses the maximum of all nesting depths.
329:         self.check_nesting_depth(&metrics, source, &mut diagnostics);
330: 
331:         // MDEEP: Parentheses/brackets nested too deeply.
332:         self.check_paren_depth(&metrics, source, &mut diagnostics);
333: 
334:         // DEEPN: Functions nested too deeply.
335:         self.check_function_depth(&metrics, source, &mut diagnostics);
336: 
337:         // DEEPS: Statements nested too deeply.
338:         self.check_statement_depth(&metrics, source, &mut diagnostics);
339: 
340:         // EOFMI: Incomplete file (last node is ERROR or MISSING).
341:         self.check_incomplete_file(&metrics, source, &mut diagnostics);
342: 
343:         // -- Line-based checks --
344: 
345:         // TEXTL: Text too long.
346:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_line_lengths(source));
347: 
348:         // DEEPC: Block comments nested too deeply.
349:         diagnostics.extend(self.check_nested_block_comments(source));
350: 
351:         // -- Post-hoc diagnostic count check --
352: 
353:         // TMMSG: Too many diagnostics generated.
354:         // NOTE: This counts diagnostics emitted by THIS rule only. The linter
355:         // may also enforce this at a higher level across all rules.
356:         self.check_diagnostic_count(source, &mut diagnostics);
357: 
358:         // -- No-op checks (handled elsewhere, documented here for completeness) --
359:         // QUIT:  Analysis did not complete — engine panic guard (catch_unwind in
360:         //        Linter::lint), emitted when an internal analyzer error occurs.
361:         // NOFIL: File not found — CLI handles file discovery.
362:         // RDERR: Unable to read file — CLI handles I/O errors.
363: 
364:         diagnostics
365:     }
366: }
367:

369: // Helpers
370: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
371: 
372: /// Find the last (rightmost, deepest) descendant node in a tree.
373: pub(crate) fn last_descendant(node: Node) -> Option<Node> {
374:     let child_count = node.child_count();
375:     if child_count == 0 {
376:         return Some(node);
377:     }
378:     let last_child = node.child(child_count - 1)?;
379:     last_descendant(last_child)
380: }

2: //!
3: //! This module implements a file-level rule engine that detects unused variables,
4: //! functions, and dead code in MATLAB source files. It covers 17 distinct check IDs

177:         for write in &field_writes {

179:             if !field_reads.contains(&key) {

200:         if self.is_check_disabled("MSNE") {
201:             return;
202:         }
203: 
204:         let mut field_writes: Vec<FieldAccess> = Vec::new();
205:         let mut field_reads: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
206: 
207:         Self::collect_field_accesses(
208:             ctx.tree.root_node(),
209:             ctx.source,
210:             &mut field_writes,
211:             &mut field_reads,
212:         );

214:         // Group writes by object name.
215:         let mut writes_by_object: HashMap<&str, Vec<&FieldAccess>> = HashMap::new();
216:         for write in &field_writes {
217:             writes_by_object
218:                 .entry(write.object.as_str())
219:                 .or_default()
220:                 .push(write);
221:         }
222: 
223:         // For each object with multiple fields written, check if any field
224:         // is written exactly once and never read — potential typo.
225:         for (object, writes) in &writes_by_object {
226:             if writes.len() < 2 {
227:                 continue;
228:             }
229: 
230:             let mut field_write_count: HashMap<&str, usize> = HashMap::new();
231:             for w in writes {
232:                 *field_write_count.entry(w.field.as_str()).or_insert(0) += 1;
233:             }
234: 
235:             for w in writes {
236:                 let key = format!("{}.{}", object, w.field);
237:                 if field_write_count.get(w.field.as_str()) == Some(&1)
238:                     && !field_reads.contains(&key)
239:                 {

241:                         rule_id: "MSNE",
242:                         message: format!(
243:                             "Struct field '{}.{}' is assigned once and never read (possible typo)",
244:                             object, w.field
245:                         ),
246:                         severity: Severity::Info,
247:                         byte_range: w.byte_range.clone(),
248:                         line: w.line,
249:                         column: w.column,
250:                         fix: None,
251:                     });
252:                 }
253:             }
254:         }
255:     }

257:     /// Collect field accesses (both reads and writes) from the parse tree.
258:     fn collect_field_accesses(
259:         node: Node,
260:         source: &str,
261:         writes: &mut Vec<FieldAccess>,
262:         reads: &mut HashSet<String>,
263:     ) {
264:         if node.kind() == "assignment" {
265:             // Check if LHS is a field_expression.
266:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
267:                 if lhs.kind() == "field_expression" {
268:                     if let Some(access) = extract_field_access(lhs, source) {
269:                         writes.push(access);
270:                     }
271:                 }
272:             }
273:             // Check RHS for field reads.
274:             if let Some(rhs) = node.child_by_field_name("right") {
275:                 Self::collect_field_reads(rhs, source, reads);
276:             }
277:         } else if node.kind() == "field_expression" {
278:             // A field_expression not on the LHS of assignment is a read.
279:             if let Some(access) = extract_field_access(node, source) {
280:                 let key = format!("{}.{}", access.object, access.field);
281:                 reads.insert(key);
282:             }
283:         }
284: 
285:         // Recurse into children (skip assignment children we already handled).
286:         if node.kind() != "assignment" {
287:             let count = node.child_count();
288:             for i in 0..count {
289:                 if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
290:                     Self::collect_field_accesses(child, source, writes, reads);
291:                 }
292:             }
293:         } else {
294:             // For assignments, recurse into children except LHS field_expression.
295:             let count = node.child_count();
296:             for i in 0..count {
297:                 if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
298:                     if child.kind() == "field_expression" {
299:                         if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
300:                             if lhs.id() == child.id() {
301:                                 continue;
302:                             }
303:                         }
304:                     }
305:                     Self::collect_field_accesses(child, source, writes, reads);
306:                 }
307:             }
308:         }
309:     }

312:     fn collect_field_reads(node: Node, source: &str, reads: &mut HashSet<String>) {
313:         if node.kind() == "field_expression" {
314:             if let Some(access) = extract_field_access(node, source) {
315:                 let key = format!("{}.{}", access.object, access.field);
316:                 reads.insert(key);
317:             }
318:         }
319: 
320:         let count = node.child_count();
321:         for i in 0..count {
322:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
323:                 Self::collect_field_reads(child, source, reads);
324:             }
325:         }
326:     }

392:     /// The field name (e.g., "field" in "s.field").

402: /// Extract a `FieldAccess` from a `field_expression` node.
403: pub(crate) fn extract_field_access(node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<FieldAccess> {
404:     // field_expression has an object and a field child.
405:     let object_node = node.child(0)?;
406:     let field_node = node.child_by_field_name("field")?;
407: 
408:     // Only handle simple identifier objects (not chained field access).
409:     if object_node.kind() != "identifier" {
410:         return None;
411:     }
412: 
413:     let object = source[object_node.start_byte()..object_node.end_byte()].to_string();
414:     let field = source[field_node.start_byte()..field_node.end_byte()].to_string();
415:     let pos = node.start_position();
416: 
417:     Some(FieldAccess {
418:         object,
419:         field,
420:         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
421:         line: pos.row + 1,
422:         column: pos.column + 1,
423:     })
424: }

426: /// Simple glob pattern matching supporting `*` (any sequence) and `?` (single char).
427: pub(crate) fn matches_simple_glob(pattern: &str, text: &str) -> bool {
428:     let pat: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();
429:     let txt: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
430:     glob_match_recursive(&pat, &txt, 0, 0)
431: }
432: 
433: /// Recursive glob matching helper.
434: pub(crate) fn glob_match_recursive(pat: &[char], txt: &[char], pi: usize, ti: usize) -> bool {
435:     if pi == pat.len() {
436:         return ti == txt.len();
437:     }
438: 
439:     match pat[pi] {
440:         '*' => {
441:             // `*` matches zero or more characters.
442:             for i in ti..=txt.len() {
443:                 if glob_match_recursive(pat, txt, pi + 1, i) {
444:                     return true;
445:                 }
446:             }
447:             false
448:         }
449:         '?' => {
450:             // `?` matches exactly one character.
451:             if ti < txt.len() {
452:                 glob_match_recursive(pat, txt, pi + 1, ti + 1)
453:             } else {
454:                 false
455:             }
456:         }
457:         c => {
458:             if ti < txt.len() && txt[ti] == c {
459:                 glob_match_recursive(pat, txt, pi + 1, ti + 1)
460:             } else {
461:                 false
462:             }
463:         }
464:     }
465: }

171:     }

175:         &[]

212: /// Find a `function_definition` node in the tree that matches the given byte range.
213: ///
214: /// Performs a DFS from the root, returning the first `function_definition` node
215: /// whose byte range matches.
216: pub(crate) fn find_function_node_at<'a>(
217:     tree: &'a Tree,
218:     byte_range: &std::ops::Range<usize>,
219: ) -> Option<Node<'a>> {
220:     let mut stack = vec![tree.root_node()];
221:     while let Some(node) = stack.pop() {
222:         if node.kind() == "function_definition"
223:             && node.start_byte() == byte_range.start
224:             && node.end_byte() == byte_range.end
225:         {
226:             return Some(node);
227:         }
228:         // Only recurse into nodes that overlap with the target range.
229:         let count = node.child_count();
230:         for i in (0..count).rev() {
231:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
232:                 if child.start_byte() <= byte_range.end && child.end_byte() >= byte_range.start {
233:                     stack.push(child);
234:                 }
235:             }
236:         }
237:     }
238:     None
239: }

241: /// Collect all variable names assigned in a block (shallow — only direct
242: /// assignment statements, not nested blocks).
243: pub(crate) fn collect_block_assignments(block: Node, source: &str) -> HashSet<String> {
244:     let mut assigned = HashSet::new();
245:     let count = block.child_count();

255:                         assigned.insert(name.to_string());

264:                                 }
265:                             }
266:                         }
267:                     }
268:                     _ => {}
269:                 }
270:             }
271:         }
272:     }

274: }

#!/usr/bin/env bun
/**
 * Generate mlt documentation pages from the rule docstring schema.
 *
 * Every rule module in `crates/mlt_rules/src` documents itself with a
 * standardized `//!` header docstring (see `docs/scripts/SCHEMA.md`). This
 * script reads those docstrings and emits:
 *
 * 1. **Rule pages** (`docs/rules/<slug>.md`) — one page per rule module, with
 *    metadata badges, a `## Check IDs` anchor list, and the docstring's
 *    `Rule` / `Fix` / `Examples` sections.
 * 2. **The rule index table** in `docs/rules.md` — one row per check ID,
 *    linking back to its rule page (and per-check anchor where available).
 * 3. **Data-driven check tables** — the compatibility + suggested-improvements
 *    inventories from the TOML data files.
 *
 * Modules that have NOT yet been migrated to the schema are rendered through a
 * legacy fallback so the docs stay consistent during migration.
 *
 * CLI:

5: # Syntax Errors
6:

12: ## What this engine does
13: 
14: The `SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE` rule implements the MATLAB Code Analyzer checks in the **Syntax Errors** category. All checks share one engine and are dispatched by tree-sitter node kind or by file-level traversal; each diagnostic carries the specific check ID (e.g. `SYNER`).
15: 
16: ## Check IDs

18: | Check ID | Description |

20: | `SYNER` | ERROR node detected in parse tree |
21: | `BDFIL` | File name doesn't follow MATLAB naming rules |
22: | `BADNE` | Source contains `!=` (MATLAB uses `~=`) |
23: | `BADOT` | Source contains `..` not part of `...` |
24: | `TWOCM` | Source contains `,,` |
25: | `CLIS` | class_definition in a script file |
26: | `CLTWO` | Multiple class_definition nodes in one file |
27: | `SOFOC` | Statements outside a class_definition in a class file |
28: | `SEMFU` | File has only empty statements (only `;` and whitespace) |
29: | `FNDOT` | Function name contains dots outside class methods block |
30: | `FNSWA` | Function name doesn't start with alphabetic character |
31: | `NOPAR2` | Missing closing bracket mid-file |
32: | `EOLPAR` | Missing closing bracket at end of line |
33: | `ENDPAR` | Missing closing bracket at end of file |
34: | `ENDCT` | ERROR node suggesting missing END |
35: | `ENDCT2` | An END might be missing after a block-opening keyword |
36: | `ENDCT3` | An END might be missing before a block-opening keyword |
37: | `ENDCT4` | A METHODS block or END might be missing before a function definition |
38: | `EOFMI` | File ends with ERROR node (incomplete) |
39: | `NOLHS` | Assignment with empty left side |
40: | `BADCH` | Invalid control characters in source |
41: | `BADSP` | Non-ASCII whitespace characters in source |
42: | `BADCT` | Unicode explicit directional formatting characters |
43: | `REDEF` | Same identifier used as both function name and variable |
44: | `SEPEXR` | Missing newline/semicolon between statements |
45: | `SBTMP` | Chaining outputs after parenthesis is not supported |
46: | `FVSYN` | Invalid function argument syntax |
47: | `FVACI` | Name-value arguments in cell indexing not supported |
48: | `FVACS` | Quoted string used as name in name=value syntax |
